# 05 · SEO

What HERON generates by itself, what you fill in, and how to move from an old site without losing search results. For whoever is responsible for search, a human or a content and SEO agent.

## What is generated by itself

None of this is written by hand or lies in a file: it is assembled on every build from the pages and `site.yaml`, so it does not go stale:

| What | Where from | In detail |
|---|---|---|
| `<title>`, meta description, canonical | `title` + `seo.title_suffix`, `description`, the page address | [`20` §4.2](../spec/20-data-contract.md#frontmatter) |
| Open Graph and Twitter | fields of groups 3-4, otherwise `title`/`description`/`seo.og_default_image` | [`20` §4.2](../spec/20-data-contract.md#frontmatter) |
| `sitemap.xml` | all published indexable pages, `lastmod` from `updated` | [`21` §9](../spec/21-engine.md#sitemap) |
| hreflang in `<head>` and in the map | translations by file name, `x-default` is the default language | [`20` §3](../spec/20-data-contract.md#languages) |
| `robots.txt` | `seo.robots_extra` + the `Sitemap:` line | [`21` §9](../spec/21-engine.md#robots-txt) |
| JSON-LD | type from the theme, data from the page and the `schema` block in `site.yaml`, breadcrumbs, FAQ | [`21` §9](../spec/21-engine.md#json-ld) |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` | page tree, `description`, `seo.llms_note` | [`21` §9](../spec/21-engine.md#llms-txt) |
| 301 and 410 | `redirect_from` of pages and `gone` in `site.yaml`, straight into the nginx config | [`21` §9](../spec/21-engine.md#redirects) |
| closed dev build | without `--env prod`: `noindex` on everything, `Disallow: /`, no counters | [`23`, "Engine version and site environment"](../spec/23-distribution.md#engine-version-vs-site-environment) |

## What you fill in

**On every page** is group 1 of the SEO block:

- `title` is up to 60 characters, for search results. The site suffix is added by itself;
- `h1` is for the one who has already opened the page. Not a copy of `title`;
- `description` is up to 155 characters: what the person gets on the page;
- group 2, "search queries": the engine does not read it, it is a working note: one intent, one page. Two files with one main query are a sign that they should be merged.

The other groups are as needed: your own image for social networks (3), refined markup (5), the image in the catalog and its `alt` (6), the publication date, `noindex` (7), old addresses (8).

**Once per site**, in `site.yaml`:

```yaml
site:
  domain: example.com
  name: Workshop
  name_ru: Мастерская        # value for the Russian pages
seo:
  title_suffix: " - Workshop"
  title_suffix_ru: " - Мастерская"
  og_default_image: media/og/default.jpg
  llms_txt: true
  llms_note:                 # facts about the site for AI models, by language
    en: |
      Phone for bookings: …
    ru: |
      Телефон для записи: …
contact: { phone: "…", city: "…" }
organization: { name: "…" }
schema:
  entity:                    # site-wide node: who stands behind the site
    "@type": Organization
    name: "{{ organization.name }}"
    telephone: "{{ contact.phone }}"
analytics:
  ga4: G-XXXXXXX
```

`{{ … }}` in `schema` are substitutions from the same `site.yaml`: the address and the phone live in one place and do not diverge between the layout and the markup. → [`20` §5, "The schema block"](../spec/20-data-contract.md#schema-block)

**Prices in the markup** are forbidden by default (`E020`): if the site does not show the cost on its pages, it must not leak into JSON-LD. To allow it, use `seo.allow_prices: true`.

**Update date.** `lastmod` and `dateModified` are taken from `updated` in the frontmatter, and if it is absent, from the source `build.updated_from`: `git` (the date of the last commit of the file), `file` (the file time) or `manual` (by hand only). A manual `updated` is stronger than the source: if you put it on all pages during the move, git dates stop working. The report after the build shows how many pages ended up this way. Dates go to the search engine as full ISO 8601 with a time zone: from git it is the commit time (`2026-10-17T11:30:12+02:00`), a manual day is midnight UTC (`2026-10-14T00:00:00+00:00`); on the page the caption stays a date. A date from the future and an update earlier than the publication are warnings, and with `--strict` errors.

## Languages

- A translation is a file with the same name in the language folder; hreflang and the language switcher appear by themselves.
- A translation can have its own address (`slug`); the link is held by the file name.
- One language means no hreflang, no language maps and no `llms-<lang>.txt`: nothing extra is generated.
- No translation means a warning in the report and a grayed-out language in the switcher; links to such a page from other languages lead to the version in the default language.
- If the main language is empty, the production build stops (`E021`).

## Moving from an old site <a id="migrate-from-old-site"></a>

The goal is that no indexed address returns 404.

1. **Export the old addresses** from the sitemap, Search Console, the logs.
2. **The address has moved**: put it into the SEO block of the new page:

   ```yaml
   redirect_from:
     - /old-page/
     - /%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%8F/
   ```

   Cyrillic and percent-encoding are normalized: a Cyrillic address and its percent-encoded form (the second line above is the encoded Cyrillic word "old") are one address, and the 301 works for either, with a slash and without.
3. **The address is gone** goes into `gone` in `site.yaml`. The server answers 410, and the search engine drops the address faster than after a 404:

   ```yaml
   gone:
     - /sample-page/        # exactly this address
     - /wp/*                # everything under /wp/
     - /?p=*                # the home page with the parameter p
   ```

4. **Build.** The engine checks that the old address does not match a live page, does not lead to two places and does not form a chain (`E009`), and that 410 does not overlap with pages and redirects (`E022`).
5. **Check on the image**: `scripts/site.sh <site> smoke prod` starts nginx and checks the answers 200, 404, every 301 and every 410: [06 · Build and deploy](06-deploy.md).

In detail: [`20` §2, "Old addresses"](../spec/20-data-contract.md#old-addresses-cyrillic), [`22` §6](../spec/22-deploy.md#migrate-existing-site).

## Before deploy

```bash
heron build my-site --env prod --strict
```

`--strict` turns warnings into errors: a broken link, an image without `alt` or an unfilled required relation will not go to production. The build report counts pages by markup types, so you can see that JSON-LD reached all of them.
